passages.note: Bill overview shows Carbone as prime sponsor of the ADU bill, signed into law as Chapter 196.

passages.provision_quote: A municipality with a population of more than seventy-five thousand persons shall adopt regulations that allow on any lot or parcel where a single-family dwelling is allowed all of the following:
passages.note: The chaptered text removes municipal zoning limits on accessory dwelling units but is confined to ADUs and sets no rule about subsidies, rent caps or affordable-unit requirements.
House Final Reading vote page shows his Aye and a divided tally, so the bill is not near-unanimous.

rows.reasoning: Carbone prime-sponsored and voted for HB 2720 (2024), which forces larger municipalities to allow accessory dwelling units as a permitted use and bars a list of local restrictions on them; that removes some of the "zoning limits that block private building", so it shows direction. But one ADU-only deregulation law cannot show that he would "Rely on the market to set prices and supply — at most, cut the regulations and zoning limits", and nothing here speaks to "binding rules on the private market like rent caps or required affordable units" or to "subsidies and tax breaks", so the rungs on this side are not separated.
